description: Start one structured program/argv command under Runtime supervision and return a command handle after policy, approval, and sandbox initialization succeed. Use this for commands that may outlast one tool call.

propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name or workspace-relative executable; absolute host executables require dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.args: The structured argument vector passed directly to the program. Never repeat program or its executable basename in args[0]; args starts with the first real argument.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Workspace-relative existing directory, or an absolute host directory only in dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.intent: The purpose of the command, used by Runtime when applying execution policy.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested total command-phase timeout. It remains attached to the process across later polls; Runtime returns the effective capped budget.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Use start_command for a legitimate long-running build, test, install, or program. It accepts the same flat program/args contract as run_command and never accepts an action object or nested invocation. After it returns status running, use poll_command for bounded status waits and cancel_command only when the process is no longer needed. Do not complete the task until a poll or cancel observes the terminal result. Its terminal failures use the same stable parameter, policy, approval, sandbox, exit, timeout, and runtime failure.kind values as run_command.
